subject: Request: Cross-border transfer evidence & DPF mapping — FinBeta
messages:
From: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@finbeta.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: DataPrivacy@finbeta.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: cross-border evidence and DPF mapping

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising for our latency-sensitive reconciliation flows. As part of our procurement sign-off I need to assemble a short evidence pack for our EU legal team on two items: 1) a high-level data flow mapping showing where FinBeta PII may traverse regions when calling your hosted inference API and 2) demonstrable controls that align with the EU DPF approach we plan to send to our counsel.

Concretely, could you provide: 
- a simple diagram or table showing request/response paths, any caching layers (KV cache behavior), and where logs are stored (region + retention),
- whether Redwood would rely on SCCs, DPF documentation, or a combination (and the operational fallback),
- KMS/HSM integration notes for customer keying (we may require Bring-Your-Own-Key for certain scopes), and
- a short list of sample artifacts we can include in the RFP (audit log sample, retention policy, redacted packet traces, DPA annex wording).

We don't need legal wording yet — just the evidence matrix and any attachments we can include with our vendor evaluation. Can you circle back by Wednesday EOD PT?

Appreciate it,

Jacob Lee
Senior Privacy Counsel | FinBeta

FinBeta | procurement@finbeta.com

Jacob — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (privacy/controls) and Karthik (infra) so we can assemble the artifacts.

High level plan / commitments:
- We'll provide a compact evidence pack (PDF) with a transfer mapping diagram, a table of where different categories of data may be processed (model inference, logs, metrics), and retention windows.

- On legal controls: we support SCC execution today for EU customers; we also maintain a DPF-aligned control mapping (operational and technical measures) which we can annotate against the FinBeta data flows. Where needed we'll call out fallback to a compatible model hosted in EU-only regions.

Ben and Karthik — can you each contribute: 
- Ben: sample audit log extract (redacted), SOC-2 pointer, and the retention policy blurb

Subject: RE: Initial ask: cross-border evidence and DPF mapping

Marissa / Karthik,

Attaching a preliminary set of artifacts to include in the pack (I'll upload final versions to the Drive link shortly):
- redwood_dpf_evidence_v1.pdf (summary + control mapping to DPF/SCC options)
- transfer_mapping_finbeta_spreadsheet.xlsx (row-per-data-element mapping showing processing region, subsystem, retention)
- audit_log_sample_redacted.txt (sample event lines with timestamps — PII removed)

Key notes to call out in the summary:
- Audit logs: stored in region-of-processing with a default retention of 90 days for hosted API metrics; longer retention (365 days) available under Dedicated/enterprise plans. Logs are append-only and hashed for tamper evidence.
- KV cache: ephemeral in-memory caches are used for prefix acceleration; on-disk persistence is not enabled for inference cache in our hosted product (only ephemeral spill to local SSD under heavy memory pressure; those SSDs are encrypted and wiped on instance recycle). We will include a small diagram to make that clear.
- DPF vs SCC: we treat SCCs as the contractual mechanism and maintain a DPF-control mapping that documents equivalent technical and organizational measures; where customers require, we can operate in EU-only regions and enable BYOK.

Jacob — asking for one small clarification: for the mapping sheet, can you confirm whether FinBeta treats user IDs as pseudonymous identifiers (hashed) or if you will be sending direct PII? That will change the recommended retention & masking notes.

Ben Carter
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@finbeta.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial ask: cross-border evidence and DPF mapping

Jacob — quick technical addendum (adding here for the evidence doc):

1) Routing and model locality: requests are routed by policy. For hosted customers without region pinning, routing may select nearest region; for FinBeta we recommend "region pin = EU" to avoid cross-border transfer for PII-sensitive flows. We'll include the routing policy snippet and the default fallbacks.

2) KV/Prefix caching behavior: it's designed for short-lived sequence caching; we do not persist user-derived content to durable object stores by default. In dedicated/private, customers can opt into local-only caches with guaranteed in-region persistence behavior.

3) Encryption & KMS: We support customer-provided keys via cloud KMS integrations (Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS) and HSM-backed envelopes for BYOK. We'll attach an HSM topology image (kms_hsm_diagram.png) and a short step-by-step for key rotation and emergency key revocation processes.

Uploading the infra diagram and the routing policy snippet to the shared Drive now.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
